verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes a recurring acceptance condition of 180 approved clip deliverables per month.
The client changes the monthly deliverable target to 140 and makes personal client approval the quota-counting gate; no obsolete key requires removal.
The client explicitly pauses creation of clips pending instructional materials.
The client defines the quota-counting rule for rejected clip deliverables: they remain excluded until corrected and approved.
The roughly 4-5 clips-per-day figure is project delivery guidance for staying on track, not a system behavior or concrete acceptance condition.
The client explicitly restarts full-speed work after the earlier production pause and again ties the resumed workflow to reaching 140 approved clips.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Because tomorrow is the 1-month mark and only 1 clip has been delivered despite my reaching out 3 times, I had no other option but to end the contract. The decision isn’t personal; the same standards have to apply to everyone on the team, and the milestones are there for a reason.

I’m sorry this is how it ended. I understand that life happens and that circumstances on your end may have been different, but I need clippers I can rely on to communicate—even if they only say, "I’m behind" or "I need more time."

I wish you well with whatever comes next. The door isn’t permanently closed: if you want to try again later and things look different for you, that may still be possible.

missing_event_candidates.decision_note: Ending the contract terminates the recurring monthly approved-clip obligation for this engagement; a possible future retry does not preserve the current requirement.
